title: utilz use brew removes the links before asking whether a Homebrew copy would answer, and can leave none on PATH (contract A4)
body:
`utilz use brew` removes the links in `~/.local/bin` before it asks whether a Homebrew copy would answer once they are gone. On a machine whose keg is installed but not linked, or where another copy comes first on PATH, it leaves no utilz on PATH, or the wrong one, and then prints the Homebrew install's version line as the tree the shell now reaches. Devbin's contract amendment A4 to `docs/dev-opt-brew.md` T5, agreed by the signatories on 26 Oct 2026 in intent-vc's wording, says: "`use brew` refuses, removing nothing, when no brew-managed copy would answer once the links are gone (the formula is not installed, its keg is not linked, or another copy comes first on PATH): it names each link it would have removed and the tree that link serves, why no Homebrew copy would answer, and the tool's own remedy (install or link the formula, or stay on dev or opt)."

## What

Line numbers are at `9027555d`, whose code HEAD has not changed.

- `install_verb_use brew` runs `tree=$(_install_brew_root) || return 1`, then `_install_remove_links "$bindir"` (`opt/utilz/lib/install.sh:1613-1614`). `_install_brew_root` (`:1478`) asks only that `$prefix/opt/utilz/libexec/bin/utilz` is executable (`:1484`). Homebrew keeps a keg's opt link when the keg is unlinked, so on an unlinked keg that test passes, the links go, and nothing answers.
- No name's first copy on PATH is asked about once its link is gone. The formula links every entry of the keg's bin (`bin.install_symlink Dir[libexec/"bin/*"]`, `packaging/homebrew/utilz.rb:31`), so whether Homebrew's copy answers is a question per link: each name the census removes must then resolve to the keg's copy.
- The refusals that do exist name neither the links nor the trees they serve, and their one remedy is `brew install`.

## Found

utilz-vc's read at `9027555d` on 26 Oct 2026, after hv ruled (a) through molt-vc (vc's decision 64) that Utilz's conformance to A4 goes into 2.14.4. utilz-vc saw, read-only on this Mac, that Homebrew keeps an unlinked keg's opt link, on the conflab and intent formulae. Devbin's issue 0235 is the same conformance for `devbin use brew`. This is the Design's second version: utilz-vc read the first (`91e06dc2df03` at `477f36c4`) as sound, and the points that read named are folded in here.

## Design

**Which copy counts as brew's.** The tree `_install_brew_root` names, `$prefix/opt/utilz/libexec`, which is the tree whose version line `use brew` prints. A name passes only when its first copy on PATH, once its link is gone, resolves (`_install_resolve`, every link followed) into that tree's `bin/`, each directory read by `pwd -P`. "Any tree `utilz_tree` calls brew" is not enough, since `use brew` prints that one tree's version line as the one the shell reaches. One predicate, `_install_answers_from <copy> <tree>`, answers "brew's copy answers", and bare `use` moves to it: its line "brew: no links, and <copy> (the Homebrew install) answers" (`:1519`) is printed only when the first `utilz` on PATH resolves into the tree `brew --prefix` names, found by the same finder. With no Homebrew install, or a first copy anywhere else, bare `use` prints "no links; <copy> answers, which is not the Homebrew install", as it does now. Until now it called any tree `utilz_tree` names brew the Homebrew install, so it could report brew for a copy whose version line `use brew` would not print. Bare `use` so gains a call to brew when there is no link, and a missing brew says nothing and changes nothing about its exit status.

**The finder.** `_install_brew_root`'s questions move into `_install_brew_find`, which prints nothing and answers either the prefix and the tree, or the reason there is none. `_install_brew_root` becomes that finder plus its refusals, word for word as now, so `_install_upgrade_brew` (`:1068`), its other caller, keeps what it prints, and a test pins those words. `use brew` no longer returns early on it: it takes the reason into its own refusal, which lists the links too.

**"Once its link is gone", computed without removing anything.** The coordinator filters PATH once per run: `_install_path_without <dir>` walks PATH by its separators, keeping an empty entry (the shell reads it as the current directory), and drops each entry that resolves to the link directory by `pwd -P`, never by string, so a `~/bin` that links to `~/.local/bin`, and `/tmp` for `/private/tmp`, are dropped too (utilz-vc's W3). Each name's verdict is handed the path it searches: the filtered PATH for a name whose link `use brew` removes, and `$PATH` as it stands for `utilz` with no Utilz link. The verdict runs bash's own `type -P`, the lookup `install_link_health` uses, as `$(PATH="$search"; type -P "$name")`, so the assignment empties bash's table of remembered commands before the search, and the verdict reads no ambient PATH. The drop rule is in one place, and each PATH entry is resolved once a run, not once a name.

**Which names are checked.** Every link `_install_remove_links` removes, and `utilz` itself. The census is read once, and the check and the removal take that one reading, through one predicate on a row's state (ours or broken, `_install_brew_removes`), so they cannot drift (IN-AG-HIGHLANDER-001). `utilz` is checked even when it has no link, since the version line `use brew` prints claims that brew's copy answers `utilz`; so `use brew` with no links now refuses where another copy of `utilz` comes first. The link directory is dropped only for a name whose link `use brew` removes there, and `utilz` with no Utilz link is looked up on PATH as it stands, because a `utilz` in the link directory that is not a Utilz link stays where it is and goes on answering.

**A broken link's name** takes the same rule as any other, as A4's text has it, so a broken link whose name the keg lacks blocks the switch too. That name is already stranded: the link answers nothing now, so removing it takes no answer away, and no release need ever carry the name. Its remedy is therefore to remove the dead link, never to wait for a release.

**The reasons, in the order they are decided.** Each is decided from what the tool already reads (`brew --prefix`, the opt link, `$prefix/bin/<name>` and PATH), never from Homebrew's own `var/homebrew/linked`. Homebrew's absence and the formula's hold for every name, so once either is found nothing after it is asked. Every case lands in exactly one reason:

- **Homebrew is not installed**: `brew --prefix` answers nothing. Words, as now: "Homebrew is not installed (brew --prefix answered nothing)". Remedy: "Install Homebrew, then the formula: brew install matthewsinclair/utilz/utilz".
- **There is no Utilz formula**: `$prefix/opt/utilz/libexec/bin/utilz` is not executable. Words, as now: "there is no Homebrew install of Utilz under <prefix>". Remedy: "Install the formula: brew install matthewsinclair/utilz/utilz".
- Then, for each name, against the tree the finder named:
- **The keg lacks the name**: the tree's `bin/<name>` is not there, as for a utility newer than the brew release. Words: "the Homebrew install has no <name>". Remedy, for a link into a tree: "Upgrade the formula once a release carries it: brew upgrade utilz"; for a broken link: "Remove the dead link: rm <bindir>/<name>", a line for each such link.
- Then the name's first copy on the path it searches. If it resolves into the tree's `bin/`, the name passes.
- **Another copy comes first**: the first copy is in a directory other than `$prefix/bin`, by `pwd -P`. Words: "another copy comes first on PATH: <copy>", followed by " (<tree> at <root>)" when the copy resolves to a Utilz tree's dispatcher, read by `install_tree_kind` and `utilz_tree`. Remedy: "Take each copy named above off PATH, or put <prefix>/bin before it (the sleeve's PATH order)".
- **The keg is not linked for the name**: a first copy in `$prefix/bin` that does not resolve into the tree's `bin/`, or no copy at all with `$prefix/bin/<name>` not into it. Words: "the keg is not linked for <name>: <prefix>/bin/<name> does not resolve into it". Remedy: "Link the formula into brew's bin: brew link utilz".
- **Homebrew's bin is not on PATH**: what is left, with `$prefix/bin/<name>` the keg's own and nothing answering. Words: "Homebrew's bin, <prefix>/bin, is not on PATH". Remedy: "Put brew's bin on PATH, in your shell config: eval "$(<prefix>/bin/brew shellenv)"".

**One source for each remedy.** Each brew command a remedy names is worded once, beside `print_path_remedy` in `opt/utilz/lib/common.sh`: `brew_install_command`, `brew_link_command`, `brew_upgrade_command`, and `brew_shellenv_command <prefix>`, which is the concrete `eval "$(<prefix>/bin/brew shellenv)"`. The refusal reads them, and so does every place that words the same remedy now: `print_path_remedy` (for `utilz doctor` and `utilz emacs doctor`), `_install_brew_root`'s refusal, upgrade's refusal for a tree it cannot name (`install.sh:977`), `install_refuse_keg` (`:748`), and doctor's notes on an old or missing manifest (`common.sh:1935`, `:1950`, `:1971`). What each of those prints does not change.

**The refusal.** It exits 1 and removes nothing, and every line of it goes to stderr. Its first line is "✗ use brew left the links in <bindir> as they were: <reason>", the reason being the one that holds for every name, or else "no Homebrew copy would answer once the links are gone". Then one line for each link it would have removed, in the census's order, naming the tree that link serves: "  <name> -> <tree> at <root>" from the census row, or "  <name> -> <target>, which has gone" for a broken link; then "  utilz (no Utilz link)" when `utilz` has none. A name that fails adds ": <reason>" to its line. Then each remedy its reasons call for, once, in the order above, and last, always, "  Or stay on dev or opt: utilz use dev|opt". The "<tree> at <root>" phrase is the bare report's, from one function the report and the refusal share.

**Where it lives (PFIC).** `_install_brew_verdict <name> <search-path> <prefix> <tree>` is the verdict for one name, a function of those inputs: it reads no ambient PATH, prints nothing when brew's copy would answer, and prints `<reason><TAB><words>` otherwise. The coordinator, `_install_use_brew`, reads the census once, filters PATH once, asks for the verdicts, renders, and then refuses, or removes through `_install_remove_links`, which takes the census it is handed. Bash 3.2 throughout: no arrays, so no empty-array expansion under `set -u`, and no mapfile; a list is a newline- or TAB-separated string read with `while read`.

**Tests**, in `opt/utilz/test/use.bats` and `upgrade.bats`, each red on `9027555d`'s code and green with the fix; a test that also passes on the old code is proved by a mutation.

- `make_fake_brew` mirrors the formula: the keg's `bin/<name>` links to `../libexec/bin/<name>` for every entry of `libexec/bin`, the opt link is `$prefix/opt/utilz`, and `$prefix/bin/<name>` links to `../Cellar/utilz/9.9.9/bin/<name>` for every entry. Its unlinked variant keeps the opt link and drops the `$prefix/bin` links, as `brew unlink utilz` does.
- Every use-brew test, refusals included, and every bare-use test that reaches the no-link branch, runs with `set -euo pipefail;` first, as `bin/utilz` runs, since a lookup with no hit returns non-zero inside `$(...)` on the refusal path; the refusal test at `:273` runs non-strict today. Each sets PATH itself and names the stub brew, so hv's `/opt/homebrew/bin/utilz` never answers in a test, and the run reads the same here and on CI.
- Every refusal test asserts "removes nothing" on the whole link directory, with `link_stamps` (`use.bats:309`) before and after, and runs with `run --separate-stderr`, so it asserts each refusal line on stderr and none on stdout; use.bats declares bats 1.5.0 for it, as install_guards.bats does.
- One test for each reason: no Homebrew, and no formula (the existing test at `:273`, split into a test for each); the keg lacks a name, for a link into the dev tree, whose remedy is the upgrade, and again for a broken link of that name, whose remedy is "Remove the dead link: rm <bindir>/<name>"; the keg unlinked; Homebrew's bin off PATH; and another copy first, once for one name alone (`utilz` and the other utility pass, and the refusal names the one) and once with the dev checkout's `bin/` ahead of Homebrew's, named with its tree. Each asserts the refusal's line for every link, its reason and its remedies, by name and never by count.
- `utilz` with no link: refused when another copy of `utilz` comes first, and refused when a `utilz` in the link directory that is not a Utilz link comes first.
- W3: with PATH reaching the link directory only through a link to it, `use brew` removes the links and prints the brew version line.
- The success path, the existing tests at `:253` and `:441` with PATH set: every Utilz link removed, nothing else touched, and the brew version line printed.
- Bare `use` reports brew when the first `utilz` resolves into the tree `brew --prefix` names (the test at `:290`, with the stub), and not when it resolves into a second keg. With no Homebrew at all (`INSTALL_BREW` naming nothing), it prints the not-brew line, nothing from the missing brew reaches stdout or stderr, and its exit status is what it was.
- Upgrade in brew with no formula under the stub's prefix prints `_install_brew_root`'s refusal whole and exits 1, in `upgrade.bats`. It passes on the old code too, so a mutation of the refusal's words proves it.
- Mutations, one line each, one at a time, each reversed and the tree checked back afterwards: the predicate compares the copy's own directory without resolving it (the success tests, W3 and bare `use`'s brew line go red); only `utilz` is checked (the one-name test goes red); PATH entries are dropped by string (W3 goes red); the link directory is dropped for every name (the arm with a non-Utilz `utilz` goes red); and the words of `_install_brew_root`'s install line change (the upgrade test goes red).

**Docs, in the same change.** The `use` usage text (`install.sh:1562`, with its "No link means brew" lines), `help/utilz.md:150-154` and `README.md:651-655`, each saying that `use brew` refuses, removing nothing, unless Homebrew's own copy would answer `utilz` and every name whose link it removes; and a line under 2.14.4's Fixed in `CHANGELOG.md`, citing A4 by its agreed text and devbin's issue 0235.

## Scope

For 2.14.4, on hv's ruling (a) (vc's decision 64). cc's, in the detached worktree `wt-0112` on main's head, `1b6eb078`. Its run is a heavy booked with molt-vc. The landing is by path on vc's word, checked by its change. Devbin's A4 is not on devbin's main yet (its `docs/dev-opt-brew.md` last changed at `40663691`, for A3), and the landing does not wait for it: the CHANGELOG and the landing commit cite A4 by its agreed text and devbin's issue 0235, and devbin's commit as well if it is on devbin's main by then. Size S.
